social_security.summary: Social Security included in Utah taxable income is taxed, but a nonrefundable credit equal to the flat tax rate times those benefits offsets the tax in full below income thresholds and phases out above them.
conditions: Credit, not an exclusion: flat income tax rate x Social Security in state taxable income
Reduced by 2.5 cents per dollar of modified AGI over $54,000 single, $90,000 joint or head of household, $45,000 married filing separately
Cannot be combined with the $450 retirement credit on the same return

sources.quote: each claimant on a return that receives a social security benefit may claim a nonrefundable tax credit against taxes otherwise due under this part equal to the product of: (a) the percentage listed in Subsection 59-10-104(2); and (b) the claimant's social security benefit that is included in the claimant's state taxable income for the taxable year.

public_pension.summary: Government pensions are taxed at the flat rate; only filers born on or before December 31, 1952 may claim a $450 nonrefundable retirement credit, which phases out with income.
conditions: $450 credit per eligible claimant, born on or before December 31, 1952
Reduced by 2.5 cents per dollar of modified AGI over $25,000 single, $32,000 head of household, $16,000 married filing separately
Cannot be claimed with the Social Security or military retirement credit on the same return

sources.quote: (2) Except as provided in Section 59-10-1002.2 and Subsections (3) and (4), each eligible claimant may claim a nonrefundable tax credit of $450 against taxes otherwise due under this part.
(a) "Eligible claimant" means a claimant, regardless of whether that claimant is retired, who was born on or before December 31, 1952.

private_pension.summary: Private pensions, 401(k) and IRA distributions are taxed at the flat rate; only filers born on or before December 31, 1952 may claim the $450 retirement credit, which phases out with income.
conditions: $450 credit per eligible claimant, born on or before December 31, 1952
Reduced by 2.5 cents per dollar of modified AGI over $25,000 single, $32,000 head of household, $16,000 married filing separately
Cannot be claimed with the Social Security or military retirement credit on the same return

sources.quote: (2) Except as provided in Section 59-10-1002.2 and Subsections (3) and (4), each eligible claimant may claim a nonrefundable tax credit of $450 against taxes otherwise due under this part.

military_retirement.summary: Military retired pay is offset by a nonrefundable credit equal to the flat tax rate times the retired pay included in AGI, with no age or income limit, so the state tax on it is effectively eliminated.
conditions: Credit, not an exclusion: flat income tax rate x military retirement pay in federal AGI
Nonrefundable; cannot be combined with the $450 retirement credit on the same return

sources.quote: a claimant who receives military retirement pay may claim a nonrefundable tax credit against taxes equal to the product of: (a) the percentage listed in Subsection 59-10-104(2); and (b) the amount of military retirement pay that is included in adjusted gross income on the claimant's federal income tax

notes: Utah uses credits rather than exclusions; all retirement income is in the flat-rate tax base (4.5% for 2025 per Tax Commission instructions). The Tax Commission's per-credit pages live on incometax.utah.gov, whose robots.txt disallows automated readers, so the only agency page quoted is the Retirees and Seniors index page, which lists the credits by name; the rules themselves come from the statute index. The Social Security credit thresholds quoted in conditions are those in the indexed 59-10-1042 (S.B. 71 of 2025 moved the credit to state taxable income and raised the single threshold to $54,000). Railroad retirement benefits get a separate deduction (not covered here). Military retired pay that is Survivor Benefit Plan income has a related survivor-benefits credit.
